body_long:
Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts has unveiled a new Private Jet Experience for 2028, called Coastlines & Culture. The group announced the itinerary from Toronto on 10 November 2026.

## The journey

The trip runs from 6 to 26 May 2028 for just 48 travellers, aboard a custom-configured Airbus A321neo-LR with an all-premium cabin, operated by Titan Airways. The programme is operated and sold by TCS World Travel. A dedicated Journey Team, including a concierge, an executive chef and a journey physician, travels with the guests.

The route leaves San Francisco for Seoul, with a visit to Jingwansa Temple, then Hangzhou and Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake, with a day trip to Shanghai alongside the historian Patrick Cranley. It continues to a private cinnamon estate in Sri Lanka, then to Four Seasons Resort Zanzibar, which is still to open, and to Sharm El Sheikh, with a private yacht charter.

## A European finale

The last chapters are written in Europe. Guests stay at the Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel, with a chartered yacht day to Cannes, before ending at Four Seasons Hotel Hampshire, with exclusive access to Hampton Court Palace.

Five hotels appear on a Four Seasons Private Jet itinerary for the first time, including San Francisco, Hangzhou, Sharm El Sheikh, Hampshire and Zanzibar. No price has been disclosed.

For Marc Speichert, Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer, a new itinerary "requires immense thought and care". Four Seasons is led by President and CEO Alejandro Reynal.

Seats also remain on four 2027 journeys: International Intrigue, New World Icons, World of Adventures and Ancient Explorer.

## The signal

Announced eighteen months ahead, the journey turns a collection of hotels into a single product. Each property becomes a chapter, and the Riviera and the English countryside are given the final word. For the hotels on the route, it is a showcase to a small group of the brand's most loyal guests.

title: Four Seasons unveils its 2028 Private Jet journey, with a European finale
